details: A star witness forces one membership query per spoke.
proof: On a projected $d$-star with centre $h_0$ and leaves $h_i$ differing from $h_0$ only at $x_i$, an identification algorithm must query every $x_i$: if it omits $x_i$, the answers are identical for $h_0$ and $h_i$.  Hence the membership-query complexity of that projection is at least $d$.  Maximizing over projections gives $\mathrm{Q}_m^p(\mathcal H)\ge\mathrm{S}(\mathcal H)$.
name: Projected Membership Queries Complexity / Star number
witness_verification: For the family #classes/halfintervals with n>=4, the established endpoint values or bounds, in parameter order, are $\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ and $2$. The first parameter divided by one plus the second tends to infinity as n tends to infinity, ruling out every reverse affine-linear bound. See the database-owned value proofs for these two endpoints.
